threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: Saying you take the tube instead of the overground for a quick trip to Shoreditch is a dead giveaway. Locals know the tracks and times like the back of their hand.
Caught a night bus from Brixton, overheard a guy arguing with a mannequin he thought was his mate. Only in London, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was really in Neukölln when I saw an old man in a bathrobe arguing with a pigeon over the last piece of bread on the sidewalk.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a kebab shop doubling as an art gallery, where the döner is served alongside rotating local artwork. Uniquely Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from the Mission when they bring their own reusable straw to the taco truck; the metal ones have a certain flair around here.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a bus that stopped for 10 minutes while the driver scolded a passenger for not having exact change. Classic Tenderloin chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is just for Gaudí sights. They miss the hidden plazas where locals share a quiet vermut on a weekday afternoon.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they struggle with the metro ticket machines, staring confusedly at the screen like it's an alien artifact.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 149 bus is a reliable way to get home after 10 PM. Welcome to Dalston, mate, good luck with that!
Last night on the 59, a man pulled out a whole roast chicken from his bag and shared it with the driver. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I stumbled upon that hidden café on a side street, its walls covered in local art and the smell of fresh bread wafting out. Never knew such gems existed.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you sip a beer while watching a public art protest on the same corner where kids are playing hopscotch. It's a wild mix.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they dodge tourists on Valencia without breaking stride—those city slickers don't even glance up from their phones.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy offer his seat to a toddler on Muni today; the kid just blinked and stared—sanctuary city moment in a hectic commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals love loud street parties, but many of us just want a quiet evening with a book, especially after a week of extra noise.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them easily; they’re the ones still holding a map upside down while navigating the Plaça del Sol.
